summary: Customer requests tamper-evident audit bundle + per-request billing reconciliation and on-call playback harness
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a discrepancy between their invoice for Feb 24-26 and the audit events delivered to their SIEM. They expect per-request token usage mapping and an auditable bundle to substantiate billing. Impact: potential billing dispute and regulatory review. Environment: prod us-east-1; enterprise tenant: MagnaFinance (enterprise). Steps to reproduce observed mismatch: 1) Customer queried their billing dashboard for Feb 24-26 and saw 1,247,532 total tokens. 2) Customer pulled their SIEM snapshots for same period and counts differ by ~18% (missing/merged events). 3) Customer attempted to replay events by session_id but encountered resume-token gaps and sequence duplicates. Logs/observations: support:request ID 0x7a3f available; sample error in bridge logs: "seq-gap: expected 00012ff, got 0001308"; SIEM human-friendly symptom: missing per-request metadata (token_count) in ~22% of events. Request: 1) Provide a tamper-evident audit bundle covering 2026-02-24 00:00:00 -> 2026-02-26 23:59:59 UTC with per-event token_count and parent-request mapping. 2) Deliver per-batch manifest with RFC3161 timestamps and ed25519 signatures (per-tenant). 3) Supply resume tokens and a lightweight playback harness (curl/snippet + container image) that can replay events in chronological order filtered by session_id and attach inferred token sums. 4) Provide a reconciliation CSV mapping request_id -> event_id(s) -> token_count used in billing pipeline and an explanation of any dedup/aggregation steps the pipeline performs.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer uses billing UI to export token usage for tenant MagnaFinance for 2026-02-24..2026-02-26
Customer compares exported token totals to SIEM snapshot delivered via earlier SUP ticket and notes 18% shortfall
Customer attempts to replay events via supplied resume token and observes sequence gap errors
Customer opens ticket requesting signed audit bundle + reconciliation mapping

comments: 2026-03-09 Aisha Kapoor (Support): Customer reported mismatch between billing tokens and SIEM-delivered events; asking for signed bundle and reconciliation mapping for Feb 24-26.

2026-03-10 Jared Millar (SRE): Acknowledged. Initial hypothesis: compaction/aggregation in billing pipeline removed per-event token_count fields upstream of export. Will verify ingestion logs and SIEM bridge batching behavior.
2026-03-10 Customer (MagnaFinance - Matthew Lin): We need legal-grade proofs (timestamps + signatures). Please include curl snippet so our auditors can download and verify checksums.

2026-03-11 Jared Millar (SRE): Collected first-pass hashes for Feb 24; requesting a short window replay to validate resume tokens. Scheduling a live call with customer and on-call for Tue 2026-03-12 17:00 UTC.
investigation_notes: Checked SIEM bridge logs: observed intermittent batch reordering between 2026-02-24T14:00 and 2026-02-25T15:00 UTC causing duplicate suppression in downstream delivery
Billing pipeline compaction: aggregator may merge low-cardinality streaming events into summaries and drop per-event token_count field (codepath in billing-aggregator v2.3)
Resume token gaps align with bridge restarts caused by a transient autoscaler event on 2026-02-25 14:31 UTC (link: slack://channel/#incidents thread id 23abc)
Confirmed that raw events in audit-store still contain token_count; only the billing-aggregator artifact drops it during compaction
resolution_notes: Provided customer with on-demand S3 bundle (presigned URL) containing: 1) NDJSON of raw events with token_count for requested window, 2) per-batch manifest.csv with SHA256 checksums, 3) ed25519-signed manifest.sig and RFC3161 time-stamp token (tsr.rfc3161)

Delivered reconciliation CSV mapping request_id -> event_id sequence -> token_count and a short README explaining how billing-aggregator v2.3 compacts events and how token sums are computed from raw events vs summaries

Shared a lightweight playback harness docker image (registry.redwood/internal/audit-playback:20260311) and a curl/snippet for auditors to stream events in chronological order with resume tokens. Example: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n 'https://s3.presigned.redwood/audit/magna-123/2026-02-24_2026-02-26.ndjson' | jq .

Workaround for immediate audit: enabled per-tenant export hook to emit non-compacted events for one-week rolling window; set retention to 7 days for MagnaFinance; billing team to re-run reconciliation and apply credit if required

Follow-up action: engineering to add a gate in billing-aggregator that retains token_count in exported summaries (ENG-issue: github.com/redwood-inference/billing-aggregator/issues/122) and product to propose configurable compaction policies for enterprise tenants
final_status: Provided bundle and playback harness; ongoing follow-up with billing for crediting if reconciliation shows overcharge
